title: Check
meaning: One rule the engine applies on every load, reporting each thing it finds wrong or still to do.

title: Problem
meaning: One thing a check found wrong or still to do in the loaded data. Problems are the result of a run, never stored.

title: Error
meaning: A problem that means the data is broken. `lathe check` exits 1 on any error.

title: Warning
meaning: A problem that means work is still to do. Warnings never fail `lathe check`.

title: Lathe's checks
meaning: The checks that ship with Lathe, read-only to every product.

title: Product check
meaning: A check a product adds for its own house rule, kept in its own data.

title: Refused record
meaning: Something Lathe will not load or save, reported once as a data-refused error naming the file, the line and the rule.

title: Children limit
meaning: The most children of one kind a record of a product should hold: its `max_children` setting, 15 by default.

title: Lone child
meaning: The one record a capability or a group holds, which makes the level group nothing.

title: Entities limit
meaning: The most entities an aggregate of a product should hold: its `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting, 7 by default.

title: Page
meaning: One display of the app at its own address, showing one focus.

title: Address
meaning: A path in the app and its `view` parameter, such as `/TL-LEND?view=graph`.

title: Focus
meaning: The product, domain, record or group an address shows.

title: Page stage
meaning: The one way a focus page draws its focus, full window behind the floating panels: Graph, ERD or Trace.

title: Space
meaning: One product as somewhere to work, chosen from the strip of icons at the far left of the nav.

title: Rail
meaning: The strip of space icons at the far left of the nav.

title: Stage folder
meaning: One of a domain's five stages in the nav, listing its records by kind.

title: Kind group
meaning: The records of one kind in a stage or under a parent, shown together when there are several kinds to tell apart.

title: Map
meaning: A product's tree laid out once as boxes, which focusing never moves.

title: Depth
meaning: How many levels below the focus the camera frames.

title: Tab
meaning: One of the open tabs, like a browser tab: its own focus, its own way of drawing it, and its own Back and Forward history. On the web the browser's own tabs are the tabs.

title: ERD
meaning: A domain's or an aggregate's model drawn as boxes and lines, one of the ways a page draws its focus.

title: Place
meaning: Where a person exploring is: the focus, page stage, camera, depth, kind filters, the wiki card's open and expanded state and scroll, and its own Back and Forward history. One per tab, whether the browser's own or the app's.

title: View
meaning: Somewhere in an interface a person uses, which presents commands and queries, with where to find it and its view requirements.

title: Endpoint
meaning: The way in that exposes one command or query to other programs, with its API requirements and handler.

title: Integration
meaning: An outside system the product exchanges with, through its adapter.

title: UI component
meaning: The code that draws the views it renders, and does what the view requirements it is linked to say.

title: Endpoint handler
meaning: The code that answers one endpoint: it runs the command or query the endpoint exposes and returns its result.

title: Adapter
meaning: The code that talks to one outside system, for the software that depends on it.

title: Domain
meaning: An area of the business with its own model and language: a product is split into domains, each owning its records end to end.

title: Aggregate
meaning: A cluster of entities changed together as one unit, by one change at a time; one of them is its root, which it is named for, and the others are its children, reached only through the root.

title: Domain event
meaning: A fact that something happened to an aggregate.

title: Command
meaning: A request to change one aggregate, aimed at the entity it changes and carrying the values the change needs; it is accepted whole or refused with every reason, and changes nothing else.

title: Value object
meaning: A value with no identity, such as an amount of money or an email, defined by its fields and checked by its constraints.

title: Specification
meaning: A named yes-or-no rule over aggregates of one domain, which commands test before they act and queries select by.

title: Read model
meaning: Data kept in the shape someone needs to read it, copied from aggregates or worked out from domain events, and never changed directly.

title: Entity
meaning: A thing the domain keeps track of, with an identity of its own; its fields are typed by a basic type, a value object or the ID of another cluster's root.

title: Invariant
meaning: A rule an aggregate always keeps, enforced by its rule before every save and shown to hold by its test.

title: Repository
meaning: The one way an aggregate is loaded and saved whole, one per aggregate.

title: Capability
meaning: A lasting ability of the business that groups a domain's use cases, in order, and names the business outcomes it is for.

title: Policy
meaning: A reaction under the command it runs, which hears one event: when that happens, run this command.

title: Query
meaning: A question asked of one read model; it changes nothing.

title: Reader
meaning: How a query reaches its read model's stored data: the one code that knows where it is stored.

title: Projection
meaning: The code that builds a read model and keeps it current as its sources change; the only code that writes it.

title: Query handler
meaning: The code that answers a query through its reader.

title: Command handler
meaning: The code that carries out a command: it loads its aggregate through the aggregate's repository, holds it to the aggregate's rules and to the specifications the command names, saves it, and raises the domain events something hears.

title: Invariant rule
meaning: The code that enforces one invariant, named as its refusal names it: the aggregate's commands run it before every save, and every load runs it over all data. An invariant is enforced by its invariant rule, and built only through it.

title: Storage requirement
meaning: What the business needs kept of one aggregate or read model, and how well: whether it survives a restart, is saved whole or not at all, how long it is kept, how it is recovered and how much of it there is. It is met by the data store its repository or reader keeps it in.

title: Data model
meaning: An entity in code: its data, its behavior and how its table stores it, one per entity.

title: Value type
meaning: A value object in code: the type that shapes its value and the code that holds it to its constraints.

title: Event type
meaning: A domain event in code: its fields and how it is delivered to what hears it.

title: Event handler
meaning: The code that hears one domain event and runs its policy's command.

title: Workbench
meaning: The wide-display layout: panels set apart on the shell, the room between them a resize handle.

title: Panel
meaning: A box that floats over the drawing of what is shown, which a person shows, hides and resizes: the navigation, the tab panel or the wiki card.

title: Keymap
meaning: The one list of keyboard shortcuts and what each does, which every key, the palette, the sheet and every hint read.

title: Theme
meaning: A named set of token values with a light set and a dark set.

title: Color mode
meaning: System, Light or Dark: which of every theme's two sets shows.

title: Product folder
meaning: A folder with a Lathe configuration or a data folder, which Lathe opens.

title: Product window
meaning: One desktop window showing one product folder.

title: App server
meaning: What a window or `lathe serve` runs Lathe from.

title: Refusal reason
meaning: One reason the store refused a command or a load: the rule broken and where.

title: Record
meaning: One thing of a kind in a product's specs: an ID unique across every kind, a title, typed fields, and at most one other record it sits under.

title: Kind
meaning: A sort of thing a product's specs describe, with its own fields and the shape of its IDs. Lathe has fifty; a product may declare more.

title: Parent
meaning: The one record a record sits under, named by one of its kind's parent fields.

title: Part
meaning: Something a record owns that is no record itself, such as an entity's fields, removed with it.

title: Link
meaning: One connection of a relation, joining two records of one product.

title: Relation
meaning: A sort of connection between two records, with the pairs of kinds it may join and its words read both ways.

title: Data file
meaning: The files in the data folder, named for what they hold: everything of one kind, one of its parts or one relation's links, one per line, sorted by key. The source of truth, reviewed in git.

title: Product
meaning: A set of specs about one piece of software, kept apart from every other: nothing in it points outside it.

title: Stage
meaning: One of the six steps of work, in order, that every kind belongs to, from discovery to the test plan.

title: Product kind
meaning: A kind a product declares for itself, in any stage, under any kind.

title: Reference
meaning: Every kind, relation, stage and check of a product, with the fields of each, generated from its schema and checks.

title: Refusal
meaning: A command the store does not accept, with every reason and no data changed.

title: Business outcome
meaning: A measurable change in the world that the product exists to bring about, for the people who use it: stated with its measure and a target by a date, measured by its tests or records, or outside the code when they can't.

title: Extension record
meaning: A record of a kind a product declares for itself, held to its kind's declaration.

title: Interface
meaning: A way the product is used: an app a person works in, calls other programs make, a terminal or an agent's tools.

title: Role
meaning: Who acts in the product's use cases, such as the Owner or an Agent.

title: Essential complexity
meaning: Complexity that comes from the question being solved: the rules, distinctions and relationships any correct solution has to capture, whatever it is made with. It exists in the world before the software, and would still have to be true if the solution were made a completely different way. It is relative: what one piece of software takes as its means, another takes as its question.

title: Accidental complexity
meaning: Complexity that comes from the means used to make a solution: tools, structure, representation and conventions the question does not require. Different means could change, reduce or remove it without changing what the solution does.

title: Provided
meaning: Decided once outside the product, for everyone who uses it, by a dependency, a platform or a generic subdomain whose essential complexity it is, so the product neither builds nor proves it itself.

title: Journey
meaning: An ordered string of use cases, of one or more actors and any domains, with the policies the product runs between them, from a trigger in the world to a result a business outcome measures; a use case is one sitting of one actor, a journey the goal several of them reach in turn.

title: Handoff
meaning: A step of a journey the product takes itself, between two actors: a policy it carries out, whenever an event, then a command.

title: Technical record
meaning: The one record of a technical kind that implements a design record, naming its file.

title: Standard
meaning: Rules that hold across the product, of one of two types: a quality, what its people need whatever it is made with (essential complexity), or engineering, how its code is made (accidental complexity). Technical records meet them and standard rule tests prove them.

title: Table
meaning: Where an entity's or read model's records, or a domain's links, are stored, with its storage and keys.

title: Entry point
meaning: A file that starts the product or one of its processes, named as in code.

title: Tooling
meaning: A script or configuration that builds, lints or tests the product, named as in code.

title: Data store
meaning: Where data actually lives, named as in code or config: a data server, a bucket, a folder of files, the browser's storage or a program's memory, kept by the software itself or by a service someone else runs.

title: Obligation
meaning: A rule a product must design, build and prove: a constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, UC requirement, view requirement, API requirement, pattern rule or standard rule, or a product's own obligation kind.

title: Designed
meaning: An obligation whose design is specified: a flow step fulfills the UC requirement, or a technical record implements the design record.

title: Built
meaning: A designed obligation every technical record implementing which names a file that exists.

title: Proved
meaning: An obligation with a test, automated or manual, at a level its kind allows.

title: Gap
meaning: An obligation that is not yet designed, built or proved, reported as a warning.

title: Run by
meaning: How a test runs: its level, its state, and its file or the reason it is manual.

title: Not automated yet
meaning: A test written before its code exists, to show what will prove an obligation. It never counts as proof.

title: Follower
meaning: A domain or use case that follows a pattern.

title: Owed
meaning: A pattern rule a domain must prove for itself, because it follows the rule's pattern.

title: Trace
meaning: The records that design, build and prove one obligation, and the files they name.

title: Serves
meaning: What a record does for a business outcome when a use case whose capability is for that outcome reaches it: worked out from the records on every read, never written down. A capability serves the outcomes it names.

title: Designed, built, proved
meaning: An obligation's three states: its implementation specified, every technical record of it naming a file that exists, its test written at a level its kind allows.

title: Test data set
meaning: The starting records, environment and accounts some tests need, made with its aggregate's own commands.

title: Pattern
meaning: Behavior several use cases share, stated once: what never varies, the settings each use case or domain that follows it answers (the known ways it varies) and its slots (the open-ended ones), so what it repeats is derived rather than written again.

title: Use case
meaning: One goal one actor sets out to finish in one sitting, which leaves something the business cares about true: not a step of a bigger goal, nor a string of several goals. It holds the requirements it must keep and the tests that show it is met.

title: UC requirement
meaning: One rule a use case must keep, stated with MUST, SHOULD or MAY, fulfilled by its flow's steps and shown to hold by its tests.

title: Flow
meaning: How a use case is carried out, whatever the interface, as ordered steps on their paths, each invoking at most one command or query; each interface that offers the use case has its own version of it, derived.

title: Slot
meaning: A point in shared behavior where what varies is open-ended, so no setting can choose it: code written by hand against a contract stated in one sentence goes there.

title: Fill
meaning: Code written by hand at a slot, against its contract: accidental complexity recorded where it is needed, and debt until what the fills of one slot repeat is stated once and derived.
